hotel-acquisition-sustainable-earnings-r.title: 收购酒店前，怎样判断账面利润能否持续？
hotel-acquisition-sustainable-earnings-r.titleEn: Before Acquiring a Hotel, How Can You Assess Whether Reported Earnings Are Sustainable?
hotel-acquisition-sustainable-earnings-r.description: 收购酒店前，要逐项核实报表利润，判断哪些能够在接手后延续，再据此确定估值测算的经营利润起点。一张真实的报表能够说明过去发生了什么，却不能单独证明换了业主以后，同样的利润还会出现。
hotel-acquisition-sustainable-earnings-r.descriptionEn: Before acquiring a hotel, verify reported earnings item by item, assess which elements can continue after the takeover, and use that assessment to establish the operating earnings starting point for valuation. An accurate set of accounts can show what happened in the past. On its own, it cannot prove that the same earnings will recur under a new owner.
hotel-acquisition-sustainable-earnings-r.author: 迈创兄弟C&T（MarvelBros C&T）
content: 收购酒店前，要逐项核实报表利润，判断哪些能够在接手后延续，再据此确定估值测算的经营利润起点。一张真实的报表能够说明过去发生了什么，却不能单独证明换了业主以后，同样的利润还会出现。
卖方展示了一个盈利年份，买方很容易接着问：按这个利润，价格相当于多少倍、几年能够回本？但如果当年有一笔不会再来的收益，或者恰好享受了即将到期的费用优惠，算出来的倍数再精确，也可能建立在错误的起点上。
## 先说清楚，双方谈的是哪一种利润
核对之前，先把利润的范围和口径写在纸上。是酒店经营层面的利润，还是持有酒店的公司净利润？覆盖哪个期间？是否已经扣除租金、品牌费用和管理费用？公司层面的融资、税费和其他业务是否混在其中？
这些问题没有统一答案，却必须有双方都能核对的答案。尤其不能拿扣除租金前的数字，与另一家扣除租金后的数字直接比较；也不能把酒店经营指标换个名称，就当作业主可分配的现金。

公开交易中能看到这种口径差异。[DiamondRock](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1298946/000129894626000010/exhibit9914q2025.htm)在2026年2月26日公布的2025年全年业绩中披露，华盛顿市中心威斯汀酒店的出售价格，相当于其2024年Hotel EBITDA的11.2倍；剔除一次性物业税抵免和临时加盟费优惠后，同一价格对应的倍数变成11.9倍。这里的Hotel EBITDA是公司披露的酒店经营指标，并非净利润。
交易价格没有因此变化，变化的是用来比较价格的利润。这个案例能说明，临时利好会影响估值所用的利润基线；它不能证明国内酒店应该采用哪一个倍数，更不能替某家酒店算出合理报价。
## 调整应当有增有减，每一笔都要问能否延续
对一次性收益，先确认它是否已经计入选定的利润起点，再判断接手后是否还会发生。某笔补偿、资产处置收益或临时减免，不能只因已经收到账款，就自动进入未来每年的经营预测。反过来，如果它本来就没有计入所用利润，再扣一次也会造成错误。
对卖方提出加回的费用，核对要同样严格。确有证据证明与持续经营无关、接手后不再发生的支出，可以列入调整讨论；但凭证上写了“一次性”，并不足以证明以后不再发生。
例如，一家酒店每年维修的设备不同，不能因此把每一年的维修都解释为偶发事项。只要维持现有服务仍然需要持续投入，就应核实相应的正常费用或资本投入，而不是把支出从未来预测中全部拿掉。具体如何列支，需要财务和工程资料支持。
临时优惠也不能一律剔除。如果有效合同确认买方可以承接优惠，且优惠覆盖拟预测的期间，应按实际期限测算；到期后的费用恢复另列。若优惠是否可承接尚未确认，就保留“继续优惠”和“恢复收费”两个情景，不把其中一个提前当成事实。

关联方支持尤其需要追到合同。卖方集团提供的办公、人事、采购或物业服务，接手后是否继续、收费如何变化，都应有书面依据。IFRS基金会对[IAS 24](https://www.ifrs.org/issued-standards/list-of-standards/ias-24-related-party-disclosures/)的官方说明提醒，关联方关系及交易可能影响损益；这只能提示核查，不能证明某笔关联交易不合理，更不能自动给出调整金额。
买方团队认为以后能提高房价、减少人员或降低采购成本，也不应直接混入历史利润调整。那是尚待实现的改善计划，需另外列出投入、权限、验证时间和失败情景。卖方过去赚到的钱，与买方希望将来多赚的钱，应能分别看清。
## 用一笔简单算例检查调整方向
以下是一组假设数字，仅用于演示核对方法，不代表真实酒店或行业标准。假设双方选定的年度经营利润为500万元，其中已经包含40万元不会延续的收益，以及30万元下一年度到期且不再续享的费用优惠；同时已经扣除20万元经核实不再发生、且无需替代投入的费用。
在其他条件不变的假设下，500万元减去40万元，再减去30万元，加回20万元，得到450万元。这个数字只是在假设条件下调整后的经营利润，不能直接称作可分配现金，也没有包含买方未来改善经营的增益。
真实项目中，最值得核对的往往不是算术，而是每一项假设：40万元是否真的计入起点？30万元优惠是否确定不能承接？20万元费用消失后，有没有同类支出需要补回来？任何一项答案改变，都应回到表里修改，不能只在会议上口头解释。
## 利润核对完，还要走到现金

利润可以按正确口径调整，现金仍可能受到应收款、付款时点和后续投资的影响。IFRS基金会对[IAS 7](https://www.ifrs.org/issued-standards/list-of-standards/ias-7-statement-of-cash-flows/)的官方说明将经营、投资和筹资现金流分别处理，并说明由利润调整到经营现金流时，需要处理非现金项目和收付时间差。这是区分利润与现金的方法依据，不是对国内某个项目的会计处理结论。
对收购判断而言，应把维持经营所需的资本开支、营运资金变化和融资安排接着列明。比如，尚未收回的应收款会影响资金安排，积欠的设备更新也可能形成后续支出；但是否属于交割调整、未来经营现金变化或收购价格条件，要结合交易结构和原始资料判断。
同一项支出不能既在利润里扣除，又不加说明地在现金测算中再扣一次。已经计入历史费用、尚未支付的款项，也不能因为现金尚未流出，就再当成一笔新的经营费用。各张表之间应能说明衔接关系。
## 把争议落到一张能追溯的核对表
配套的“酒店收购利润核对与调整表”可作为记录底稿。先写明酒店及经营主体、期间、原始报表名称和利润口径，再按项目逐行核对。每行至少记录：原报表项目及金额、是否已计入起点、拟调整方向及金额、为什么调整、原始证据位置、接手后是否持续、待核问题和负责确认的人。
表尾另列资本开支与营运资金的后续现金影响，并注明它们进入哪一张测算表，防止重复计算。若使用不同币种、含税口径或不同期间的数据，也要先统一比较基础。
每一行只设清楚的处理状态。有凭证、合同及期间对应关系支持的，列为“已证实”；仍欠缺承接确认、合同或原件的，列为“待核实”；依据不足或重复计算的，列为“不接受本次调整”。不接受调整请求，不等于认定原报表虚假；它只表示目前不能据此改变估值起点。
财务负责人牵头把调整与原报表对上，经营团队解释费用用途和服务后果，合同负责人核实权利义务能否延续；涉及设备和维修时，由有相应能力的人员补充核验。买方投资负责人决定哪些待核项影响继续谈判、补证或报价条件，不能把这个责任交给卖方的调整表。
在第一次依据利润讨论报价前，可以先做一次范围有限的核对：从最近完整经营年度中选出金额较大、波动异常或被要求加回的项目，逐笔追到凭证、合同和收付款记录。选取范围应结合项目规模及对报价的影响确定，不设所有酒店通用的金额或比例。
判断核对是否有效，要看原报表与调整后利润的差额能否逐项解释，重大项目是否有证据支持，同一费用是否被重复处理，以及待核项变化是否会实质改变报价判断。表格填满、会议开完，都不代表利润已经可信。
## 资料不足时，保留条件比制造确定性更有用
这套方法主要适用于已有相对完整经营记录的在营酒店。新开业、爬坡期或刚完成重大改造的项目，历史业绩未必能提供稳定基线，应另做分阶段测算，不能靠几笔加减就造出一个“正常年份”。
如果关键账款无法对上、关联支持的承接条件不明，或者卖方拒绝提供足以支持重大调整的资料，就应暂停把该项当作确定利润写进报价依据。可以保留有依据的情景或补证条件；若缺口足以影响投资判断，先停下测算结论，不能用更高的折现率掩盖基础资料缺失。

利润基线形成后，再接入[投资回报模型](/zh/lean/article/hotel-investment-roi-irr-npv-2026)；需要改造的项目，还应继续核算[资产现金流](/zh/knowledge/hotel-renovation-asset-repricing-2026-08-21)和投入安排。收购讨论的第一步，是把一张有证据、有待核项、有责任人的利润核对与调整表摆到桌上，让双方先确认：准备拿来估值的这笔利润，究竟靠什么延续。
contentEn: Before acquiring a hotel, verify reported earnings item by item, assess which elements can continue after the takeover, and use that assessment to establish the operating earnings starting point for valuation. An accurate set of accounts can show what happened in the past. On its own, it cannot prove that the same earnings will recur under a new owner.

When a seller presents a profitable year, a buyer may quickly ask what multiple the price represents and how many years it will take to recover the investment. But if that year includes income that will not recur, or benefits from a fee discount about to expire, even a precisely calculated multiple may rest on the wrong starting point.
## First, define which earnings both sides are discussing

Before reviewing the figures, write down the scope and definition of earnings. Are they earnings from hotel operations, or the net profit of the company that owns the hotel? Which period do they cover? Have rent, brand fees and management fees already been deducted? Are company-level financing, taxes or other businesses included?

There is no single answer to these questions, but the answers must be verifiable by both sides. In particular, a figure before rent cannot be compared directly with another hotel's figure after rent. Nor does renaming a hotel operating metric turn it into cash available for distribution to the owner.

A public transaction illustrates the difference. In its full-year 2025 results released on 26 February 2026, [DiamondRock](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1298946/000129894626000010/exhibit9914q2025.htm) disclosed that the sale price of The Westin Washington, D.C. City Center represented 11.2 times its 2024 Hotel EBITDA. Excluding a one-time property tax credit and a temporary franchise fee discount, the same price represented 11.9 times Hotel EBITDA. Hotel EBITDA here is the hotel operating metric disclosed by the company, rather than net profit.

The transaction price did not change; the earnings used to compare that price did. The example shows how temporary benefits can affect the earnings baseline used in valuation. It does not establish which multiple a hotel in China should use, or determine a reasonable offer for any particular property.
## Adjustments can run in both directions; ask whether each item will continue

For non-recurring income, first confirm whether it is already included in the selected earnings starting point, then assess whether it will recur after the takeover. Compensation, a gain on an asset disposal or a temporary concession should not automatically enter every future year's operating forecast simply because the money has been received. Conversely, deducting an item that was never included in the selected earnings figure would also be wrong.

Apply the same scrutiny to expenses the seller proposes to add back. An expense may be considered for adjustment if evidence shows that it is unrelated to ongoing operations and will not recur after the takeover. A document labelling it “one-time” is not sufficient evidence that it will disappear.

For example, a hotel may repair different equipment each year. That does not make every year's repairs exceptional. If continued expenditure is necessary to maintain the existing service, the corresponding normal expense or capital investment must be verified rather than removed entirely from the forecast. The appropriate treatment requires financial and engineering evidence.

Temporary discounts should not automatically be removed either. If a valid contract confirms that the buyer can retain a discount throughout the forecast period, model it for its actual term and show the return to normal charges after expiry separately. If transferability remains unconfirmed, retain both a continued-discount scenario and a normal-charge scenario, without treating either as an established fact.

Related-party support needs particular attention to contracts. Whether office, human resources, procurement or property services supplied by the seller's group will continue, and how charges will change, should have a written basis. The IFRS Foundation's official explanation of [IAS 24](https://www.ifrs.org/issued-standards/list-of-standards/ias-24-related-party-disclosures/) notes that related-party relationships and transactions may affect profit or loss. This is a reason to investigate; it does not prove that a particular related-party transaction is unreasonable or establish an adjustment amount automatically.

A buyer's expectations of higher room rates, fewer staff or lower procurement costs should also be kept separate from adjustments to historical earnings. These are improvement plans yet to be realised. Their required investment, decision rights, validation timetable and failure scenarios should be set out separately. It should be possible to distinguish what the seller earned in the past from what the buyer hopes to earn additionally in the future.
## Use a simple calculation to check the direction of adjustments

The following figures are hypothetical and illustrate the review method only. They do not represent an actual hotel or an industry standard. Assume both sides select annual operating earnings of RMB 5 million. This already includes RMB 400,000 of income that will not continue and RMB 300,000 of fee discounts that expire in the following year and will not be renewed. It also reflects the deduction of RMB 200,000 in expenses verified as non-recurring and requiring no replacement expenditure.

Assuming all other conditions remain unchanged, subtract RMB 400,000 and RMB 300,000 from RMB 5 million, then add back RMB 200,000, to reach RMB 4.5 million. This is adjusted operating earnings under the stated assumptions. It cannot be called distributable cash directly, and it excludes gains from the buyer's future operating improvements.

In an actual project, the most valuable checks often concern the assumptions rather than the arithmetic. Was the RMB 400,000 actually included in the starting figure? Is it certain that the RMB 300,000 discount cannot transfer? When the RMB 200,000 expense disappears, will similar spending need to replace it? Any changed answer should be reflected in the worksheet, rather than explained only verbally in a meeting.
## After reviewing earnings, work through to cash

Earnings may be adjusted on the correct basis while cash remains affected by receivables, payment timing and subsequent investment. The IFRS Foundation's official explanation of [IAS 7](https://www.ifrs.org/issued-standards/list-of-standards/ias-7-statement-of-cash-flows/) distinguishes operating, investing and financing cash flows, and explains that reconciling profit to operating cash flow requires adjustments for non-cash items and differences in receipt and payment timing. This provides a methodological basis for distinguishing earnings from cash; it is not an accounting conclusion for a particular project in China.

For an acquisition decision, then identify the capital expenditure needed to maintain operations, changes in working capital and financing arrangements. Outstanding receivables, for example, affect funding needs, while overdue equipment replacement may require subsequent spending. Whether these belong in completion adjustments, future operating cash changes or acquisition price terms depends on the transaction structure and underlying records.

An expense must not be deducted in earnings and then deducted again in the cash calculation without explanation. An unpaid amount already recognised as a historical expense must not be treated as a new operating expense merely because the cash has not yet left the business. The relationship between the schedules should be clear.
## Put disputed items into a traceable review worksheet

The accompanying Hotel Acquisition Earnings Review and Adjustment Worksheet can serve as a working record. Start with the hotel and operating entity, period, original financial statement name and earnings definition, then review each item in a separate row. Each row should record at least the original statement item and amount, whether it is included in the starting figure, the proposed adjustment direction and amount, the reason, the location of original evidence, whether it continues after the takeover, outstanding questions and the person responsible for confirmation.

Record the subsequent cash effects of capital expenditure and working capital separately at the end, identifying which calculation schedule includes them to prevent double counting. Where figures use different currencies, tax bases or periods, first put them on a comparable basis.

Give each row a clear status. Items supported by vouchers, contracts and matching periods are “verified”; those awaiting transfer confirmation, contracts or originals are “pending verification”; requests with insufficient support or double counting are “adjustment not accepted in this review”. Rejecting an adjustment request does not mean the original accounts are false. It means the valuation starting point cannot currently be changed on that basis.

The finance lead should reconcile adjustments to the original accounts. The operating team explains the purpose of expenses and the service consequences, while the contract lead verifies whether rights and obligations will continue. Suitably qualified personnel should provide additional checks for equipment and repairs. The buyer's investment lead decides which unresolved items affect further negotiations, evidence requests or offer conditions. That responsibility cannot be delegated to the seller's adjustment schedule.

Before the first discussion of an offer based on earnings, conduct a limited review: select material items, unusual fluctuations and requested add-backs from the latest complete operating year, and trace each to vouchers, contracts and receipt and payment records. Set the scope according to the project's scale and potential effect on the offer, rather than applying a universal amount or percentage to every hotel.

Judge the review by whether every difference between reported and adjusted earnings can be explained, material items have supporting evidence, expenses have been counted twice, and changes in unresolved items could materially affect the offer assessment. A completed spreadsheet and a finished meeting do not establish that earnings are reliable.
## When evidence is limited, retaining conditions is more useful than manufacturing certainty

This method mainly suits operating hotels with reasonably complete operating records. A newly opened hotel, a property still ramping up or one that has just completed major renovation may lack a stable historical baseline. Such projects need phased forecasts; a few additions and deductions cannot manufacture a “normal year”.

If key balances cannot be reconciled, the terms for continuing related-party support are unclear, or the seller refuses to provide sufficient evidence for material adjustments, stop treating the item as certain earnings in the basis for an offer. Retain supported scenarios or evidence conditions where appropriate. If the gap could affect the investment decision, suspend the modelling conclusion rather than using a higher discount rate to conceal missing underlying information.

Once the earnings baseline is established, connect it to the [investment return model](/en/lean/article/hotel-investment-roi-irr-npv-2026). Projects requiring renovation also need further assessment of [asset cash flows](/en/knowledge/hotel-renovation-asset-repricing-2026-08-21) and investment arrangements. The first step in an acquisition discussion is to put an evidence-backed earnings review and adjustment worksheet on the table, with unresolved items and named responsibilities, so both sides can establish what will allow the earnings being valued to continue.
